title.narrative: Capacity building for mainstreaming social risk management in development policy and public investment in China

description.narrative: The proposed grant aims to strengthen technical and policy-coordinating capacity of the Social Development Department of China's NDRC in mainstreaming social risk management in China's development policy and public investment. COMPONENT 1: study on gradual settlement of floating population The proposed IDF grant will support a study on national policy references in addressing new challenges and issues in the settlement of floating population in China. It will prepare policy references and training materials for the NDRC in policy-guided migration with standard practice in policies, public budget allocation, access to basic social services, and issues related to migrants of new generations. This will be combined with in-depth review of four or five pilot city cases in integrating rural-urban migration and management of the floating population in various places in China. Policy reference reports and case studies will center on current policy obstacles, innovation needs and recommendations to enable the floating population settlement. Based on the study findings, tailored training materials for the NDRC will be developed. COMPONENT 2: development of a training program based on thematic studies The proposed grant will fund two thematic studies and the preparation of a training curriculum and materials on social development for the NDRC. One study will focus on the analysis of social success and failure factors in large public investments in China, based on a few case studies on the Chinese experience of social development through public investment projects. The other study will examine the Government's outsourcing services to CSOs, with Chinese and international case studies. It will also build on the findings of the previously mentioned Bank-funded TCC5 project results. Combined with the two studies' findings and existing national and international knowledge and experience, a collection of needs-based training materials on social accountability, cohesion, inclusion will be also distilled for the NDRC and will be tailored into an NDRC social development training program for future regular training. COMPONENT 3: pilot of training program and capacity building The proposed grant will support pilots of the training program developed by the proposed project. The pilot will consist of two training workshops for NDRC and provincial DRC officials in social development. Each training may receive 100 trainees. One of the workshops may be combined with the Bank-NDRC annual innovation workshop if possible; and the other training will be a stand-alone event for central and local DRC officials who will be the trainers for lower level officials in charge of social development. The trainees will improve their capacity in mainstreaming social dimensions.
